AusPak

AusPak helps a cricket analyst or fan explore how Australia and Pakistan score runs and lose wickets across the phases of a men’s One Day International (ODI) innings. It ships per-over scoring data for the 45 Australia v Pakistan ODIs in the Cricsheet archive, a function that summarises scoring by phase of the innings, and a Shiny app for exploring the results.

Question the app answers: in which part of an ODI innings does each side score fastest and lose wickets, and has that changed over time?

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-somya090997/

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-somya090997")

Launch the app 

library(AusPak)
run_app()

The app lets you choose the innings (batting first or chasing), a measure (runs or wickets per over), whether to view phases or individual overs, and a range of years. A second tab explains the fields and how to read the results.

Example

phase_summary() returns the average runs and wickets per over by phase for each team. Here, for the chasing innings in matches from 2010 to 2020:

library(AusPak)

phase_summary(aus_pak_overs, innings = 2, years = c(2010, 2020))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   batting_team phase            matches runs_per_over wickets_per_over
#>   <chr>        <fct>              <int>         <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1 Australia    Powerplay (1-10)       9          5.16           0.122 
#> 2 Australia    Middle (11-40)         9          5.06           0.0871
#> 3 Australia    Death (41+)            8          6.59           0.131 
#> 4 Pakistan     Powerplay (1-10)      15          4.58           0.127 
#> 5 Pakistan     Middle (11-40)        15          4.94           0.167 
#> 6 Pakistan     Death (41+)           12          5.89           0.443

Read the matches column alongside the averages. Late overs come from fewer matches because innings end early, so differences built on a handful of matches are weak evidence.

What is in the package

Component What it does
aus_pak_overs Per-over runs and wickets for each innings of each match, with running totals
phase_summary() Average runs and wickets per over by team and phase (or by over), for an innings and range of years
run_app() Launches the Shiny app

The data is built by data-raw/odi-overs.R, which downloads the ODI archive and keeps Australia v Pakistan matches. Phases are overs 1 to 10 (powerplay), 11 to 40 (middle) and 41 onwards (death). Wickets include all dismissal types, including run-outs.

Data source

Ball-by-ball data from Cricsheet, downloaded with the cricketdata package. Cricsheet data is shared under an open-data licence; see the Cricsheet site for its current terms.

The plot styling and the per-over summarising approach are adapted from an ETC5523 workshop.
